method: Root model inspected actual Chromium captures, compared old and redrawn Robin at the same depth, inspected complete-figure atlas contact sheet and four-frame walk source, and checked desktop and narrow minigame layouts. This is model visual review, not a human playtest.
observations: Robin retains a complete connected body and has a smaller, more proportionate head; the mature black Enies Lobby dress, bangs and boots are recognizable. Same-depth standing and walking keep a common floor anchor.
Low-foot-clearance walk frames preserve complete figures; opposite arm phases replace the rejected repeated side poses. The report separately measures all four real rendered route frames.
New supply art clearly separates food, tools and books; readable prompts and fixed selection hitboxes support the timed rounds.
Training uses a full-body character, visible step markers and separated light cues, with keyboard and 390px touch controls.
Wallet-full view explains that results are retained and can be claimed after shopping.
Final production room-to-wheel integration captures show the redrawn Robin in both challenges. Narrow supply labels and controls fit; Escape focus regression was fixed and both browser reports rerun.
limitations: Fun and character appeal remain subjective; no human player acceptance is claimed.
The narrow room is an intentional horizontal scroll surface, while its outer page remains contained.
Transparent WebP RGB data can look distorted in a decoder that ignores alpha; actual white-background composites and Chromium wood-floor captures are clean.
